pride_data.title: APEX2-based quantitative proteomic study of LAT and CD3z in Jurkat T cells
pride_data.projectDescription: TCR binding to its ligands induces a cascade of signaling starting by the phosphorylation of immunoreceptor tyrosine-based activation motif (ITAMs) present in the TCR-associated CD3 complex. This is followed by the phosphorylation of proteins including the adaptor LAT, which once phosphorylated interacts with multiple proteins allowing signal diversification and amplification downstream of the TCR. We take advantage of peroxidase-catalyzed proximity labeling combined with quantitative mass spectrometry to track the formation of CD3z and LAT interactome dynamics in Jurkat cells after TCR stimulation. We find more than 1 000 high confidence proteins for each bait and provide a quantitative molecular map of proteins enriched or reduced from the vicinity of CD3z and LAT, after stimulation. We detail and compare the recruitment kinetics of signaling proteins to CD3z and LAT and identify previously uncharacterized mediators of T cell activation. We show that the kinase MARK2, which is in the proximity of LAT and CD3z at resting state and lost upon activation, is a negative regulator of cytokine production by T cells. This study provides a resource for uncovering the complex signaling networks that regulate TCR activation and highlights new players of the TCR-induced signaling cascade.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Jurkat expressing the chimeric molecules: LAT-APEX or CD3z-APEX cells (20 × 106) were resuspended at 10× 106 cells/mL in RPMI medium + 10% FCS + 25mM HEPES + 0.5 mM Biotin-phenol (ref. LS-3500.0250, Iris Biotech) and incubated at 37°C + 5% CO2 for 1 hour. To activate the cells, we added anti-CD3 (clone OKT3, ref.317326, BioLegend) and anti-CD28 (clone CD28.2, ref.302934, BioLegend) antibodies at 4 μg/mL and incubated them at 37°C for different timepoints. One minute before the end of the activation, H2O2 was added at 0.1 mM, starting the biotin-tagging of proximal proteins. To stop the reaction, we added 2x freshly prepared cold quenching buffer 1:1 (1x = PBS with sodium azide 10 mM, sodium ascorbate 10mM [A4034-100G], Trolox 5mM [238813-5G]). Cells were then centrifuged at 400g for 3 min and washed with 4 mL of cold quenching buffer 1x 3 times. After the last centrifugation, cells are resuspended in 400 μL of Quenching lysis buffer (50mM Tris, 150 mM NaCl, 0.1% SDS, 0.5% sodium deoxycholate, 1% NP-40, 10mM sodium azide, 10 mM sodium ascorbate, 5mM trolox, protease inhibitor (cOmplete EDTA-free, ref 11873580001, Roche) and phosphatase inhibitor (Halt Phosphatase Inhibitor, ref. 78426, Thermo-Fisher Scientific)). After clearing the lysate by centrifuging at 20.000g at 4°C, we loaded the supernatant in a pre-washed Zeba Spin Desalting Column (7K MWCO, ref. 89890, Thermo-Fisher Scientific) and followed the manufacturer’s protocol to remove unreacted biotin-phenol. 10% of the lysates were kept as input and the biotinylated proteins present in the rest of the lysate were purified. 30 μL of pre-washed protease-resistant streptavidin Dynabeads M-280 were added to the samples and incubated at 4°C for 2.5 hours with gentle rotation. The beads were then washed sequentially: 2 times with quenching lysis buffer, 3 times with ammonium bicarbonate 200mM (Sigma, ref. A6141) + 6M Urea (Euromedex, ref. EU0014.A) and 5 times with ammonium bicarbonate 25 mM. Half of the beads were resuspended in 100 μL of ammonium bicarbonate 25 mM and delivered to the proteomic platform, and the other half was resuspended in 20 μL of laemmli buffer (Bio-Rad, ref. 1610747) + 2mM biotin (Sigma, ref. B4501) + 20 mM DTT (Pierce, ref. A39255) for WB analysis.  After delivery to the proteomic platform, the beads were washed trice with 100 μL of 100 mM NH4HCO3, resuspended in 100 μL of 100 mM NH4HCO3 and digested by adding 0.2 μg of trypsin-LysC (Promega) for 1 h at 37 °C. Samples were then loaded into custom-made C18 StageTips packed by stacking three AttractSPE® disk (#SPE-Disks-Bio-C18-100.47.20 Affinisep) into a 200 µL micropipette tip for desalting. Peptides were eluted using a ratio of 40:60 CH3CN:H2O + 0.1% formic acid and vacuum concentrated to dryness with a SpeedVac device. Peptides were reconstituted in 10µL of injection buffer in 0.3% TFA before LC-MS/MS analysis.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: For identification, the data were searched against the Homo Sapiens (UP000005640_9606) UniProt databases using Sequest HT through proteome discoverer (version 2.4). Enzyme specificity was set to trypsin and a maximum of two miss cleavages sites were allowed. Oxidized methionine, Met-loss, Met-loss-Acetyl and N-terminal acetylation were set as variable modifications. Maximum allowed mass deviation was set to 10 ppm for monoisotopic precursor ions and 0.6 Da for MS/MS peaks. The resulting files were further processed using myProMS v3.10.0 (https://github.com/bioinfo-pf-curie/myproms) [PMID: 17610305]. FDR calculation used Percolator 3 and was set to 1% at the peptide level for the whole study. The label free quantification was performed by peptide Extracted Ion Chromatograms (XICs), reextracted across all replicates and computed with MassChroQ version 2.2.21 [PMID: 21751374]. For protein quantification, XICs from proteotypic peptides shared between compared conditions (TopN matching) and missed cleavages were allowed. Median and scale normalization was applied on the total signal to correct the XICs for each biological replicate (N=5 in each condition). To estimate the significance of the change in protein abundance, a linear model (adjusted on peptides and biological replicates) was performed, and p-values were adjusted using the Benjamini–Hochberg FDR procedure. Max Label-free quantification (LFQ) was also performed following the algorithm as described [PMID/ 24942700] with the minimum number of peptide ratios set to 2 peptides and with the large ratios stabilization feature.
